problem: Every glyph is reflected: the font stores code 288 - ord(char). Extraction without decoding yields byte-shifted gibberish that still counts as a fat text layer.
evidence: The running head decodes as EXALTED THE OUTCASTE; chapter heads as CHAPTER ONE LOOKSHY AND THE SEVENTH LEGION and CHAPTER THREE THE FOREST WITCHES; printed folios decode to their own page numbers. The mapping is proved by the book, not inferred.
extractor: poppler (pdftotext) with -layout PLUS the column splitter, NOT pdfminer and NOT plain mode. pdfminer DROPS U+00AD (this cipher's lowercase 's'). Plain pdftotext mode reads in the right order but silently eats the line-end soft hyphens as hyphenation, losing ~7 's' per page ('hamletare' for 'hamlets are'). -layout keeps every character; the column splitter restores reading order.

0x2d.why: U+00AD soft hyphen, which poppler renders as '-'; 288-115=173. A real hyphen encodes as 0xF3 and decodes normally, so every 0x2D here is an 's'.

0x4b.why: apostrophe (raw ASCII passthrough; a real letter K arrives as 0xD5)

0x4e.why: left double quote (a real N arrives as 0xD2)

0x4d.why: right double quote (a real M arrives as 0xD3)

0x4f.why: em dash (a real O arrives as 0xD1)

0x7b.WARNING: Missing this mapping is why the first artifact batch fell back to the fan index for all 26 Outcaste ratings. Ratings are spent against the Artifact Background budget; they must come from the page. NOTE: this recovers dots printed in BODY text ('these are Artifact •••'). The dots inside artifact HEADINGS — '(ARTIFACT )' — are absent from the text layer entirely and CANNOT be recovered here; they need the VLM on the page image or a human read.
